Add space without making the home feel divided

Home additions designed to belong.

An addition changes the structure, exterior, utilities, circulation, and relationship between old and new. RT Signature Homes coordinates those decisions as a single design-build scope.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 407-6291
Design inspiration imagery · Redmond-based service

Project fit

This service is for homeowners adding bedrooms, living areas, offices, expanded kitchens, primary suites, or other conditioned space.

Typical scope

  • Feasibility, zoning, setback, and lot-coverage review
  • Architectural and structural integration
  • Foundation, framing, roofing, siding, windows, and utilities
  • Interior connection, circulation, and finish continuity
  • Permitting, inspections, and construction sequencing

Design ideas

Home Additions inspiration

Explore visual directions alongside the planning, material, and performance decisions that help turn an idea into a buildable project.

Home Addition Design Ideas

An addition should improve the existing home rather than feel attached to it. These ideas focus on massing, rooflines, openings, circulation, daylight, and material transitions between old and new.

Explore the gallery

Exterior integration

Resolve rooflines, massing, openings, and materials together.

A convincing addition respects the proportions and weather-protection strategy of the existing home.

Roof drainage, flashing, siding transitions, windows, and foundation relationships are part of the design—not cleanup decisions.

Interior connection

Make the new space improve the existing floor plan.

The opening between old and new affects circulation, daylight, furniture placement, and structural work.

The addition should solve the larger household problem rather than simply attach square footage.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Home Additions FAQs

What determines whether an addition is feasible?

Zoning, setbacks, lot coverage, utilities, structure, site access, drainage, budget, and the intended relationship to the existing house.

Can an addition be combined with remodeling?

Yes. Combining scopes can improve layout continuity and reduce duplicated disruption when the work is designed and permitted together.

Will the addition match the existing home?

The goal is intentional integration. Exact material matches may not always be available, so proportion, alignment, color, and transition details matter.
